transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jared (Redwood SE), Eva (CS), Lena (Aurora Head of Security), Tom (Identity Ops), Priya (Platform), Marcus (Compliance), Samir (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick security/compliance-focused run through for SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning and least-privilege role mapping. Confirmed Aurora's SOC 2 scope, asked about ISO intent, KMS integration, and audit log needs. Agreed next steps: send SAML metadata, SCIM playbook, map groups->roles, pilot window.

Topics: SSO SAML metadata, SCIM token lifecycle, group sync cadence, RBAC role hierarchy, least-privilege enforcement, audit logging retention, KMS key wrapping, data residency constraints, private deployment options

Transcript body:
[00:00:06] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for carving out time today. Quick round robin — if you can say name and role.
[00:00:12] Lena (Aurora): Lena Ortiz, Head of Security at Aurora. We're evaluating SSO onboarding and trying to lock down role boundaries for engineers vs product.
[00:00:18] Tom (Aurora): Tom Avery, Identity Ops. We're primarily on Okta. We'll be handling the SCIM side.
[00:00:22] Priya (Aurora): Priya Nair, platform. Interested in KMS integration and data residency implications.
[00:00:28] Maya: Great. Jared, do intro?
[00:00:31] Jared (Redwood SE): Hey all, Jared Kim. I'll walk through the SCIM flow and RBAC examples and surface some gotchas we've seen with Okta group mappings.
[00:00:40] Marcus (Aurora): Marcus Li, compliance. Quick question — we are SOC 2 Type II in scope, planning ISO later. Want to confirm audit and retention capabilities.
[00:00:48] Maya: Yep we'll cover audit logs and retention. Quick note: we'll assume you want least privilege semantics — not everyone gets cluster admin.

[00:01:20] Jared: Ok jump into SAML first. Redwood supports IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows. For Okta we usually exchange metadata — you'll upload our SP metadata into Okta and configure assertions for nameid/email and groups.
[00:01:35] Tom: For group claims do you recommend groups in the SAML assertion or SCIM-only? We have large group churn so don't want to bake it in SAML.
[00:01:45] Jared: Good question. Common pattern: use SAML for authentication + minimal attributes (email, sub, maybe primary role) and use SCIM for authoritative group provisioning. That reduces SAML token size and avoids stale claims.
[00:01:57] Lena: So SCIM is the source of truth for roles. How do you handle conflicting data if SAML contains a role claim?
[00:02:05] Jared: We prioritize SCIM for RBAC group->role mapping. If SAML role present and SCIM absent, we can accept it but we recommend a policy to treat SCIM as canonical. We can add a warning in the audit logs when role sources conflict.

[00:03:20] Priya: On SCIM tokens — how long do they live, do you support scoped tokens and IP restrictions? We want to rotate tokens and limit where provisioning calls come from.
[00:03:30] Jared: SCIM tokens are long-lived API tokens by default but you can rotate them. We support token scoped to provisioning only and you can restrict by CIDR when using Redwood Private or Dedicated in a VPC. For hosted, IP restrictions are a bit more limited; we recommend provisioning via a connector from your side if strict egress is required.
[00:03:48] Tom: Okta specifics — do you consume Okta's group pushed or pull mode?
[00:03:52] Jared: We support push from Okta (SCIM push) and also periodic pulls. Push is typical and immediate; pull mode is useful for rate-limit sensitive orgs.

[00:05:10] Lena: Let's move to RBAC. We have 6 teams: infra, platform, data, product, security, and a few contractors. We want least privilege but also flexible temporary elevation for on-call.
[00:05:22] Jared: We usually recommend a base role hierarchy: viewer -> operator -> admin. Then map Okta groups to these roles. For temporary elevation you can integrate with your existing privilege escalation (e.g., ticketing + short-lived RBAC tokens) or Redwood's canary role elevation with audit hooks.
[00:05:40] Samir: Is there built-in approval workflow or do you expect we handle it externally?
[00:05:44] Jared: Built-in approvals are basic — approve/deny flows tied to group changes. For full JIT ephemeral sessions we integrate with your existing tool (e.g., LDAP/JIT or a ticketing system).

[00:06:58] Marcus: On audit logs — what is included? We require immutable logs for all admin-level changes and user provisioning events. Retention must be at least 3 years for some parts.
[00:07:10] Maya: We emit structured audit logs for authentications, provisioning (SCIM), role changes, and admin API calls. Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) and we support log integrity checks. For hosted customers retention is configurable up to 1 year by default but enterprise add-on can extend longer. For Private/Dedicated you control retention.
[00:07:35] Marcus: Hmm 3 years is a lot — we need to understand Private options.
[00:07:39] Maya: For Private deployments you run the control plane in your VPC/on-prem and can set retention per your policy and ship to your S3/GCS or archive to cold storage.

[00:09:02] Priya: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys? We need keys for encrypting KV cache and persistent model artifacts and to ensure key rotation policies.
[00:09:12] Jared: Yes, we support KMS integration. For hosted we support external KMS with envelope encryption — customer keys wrap the data keys; for Private you can bring your own HSM or KMS. We also support key rotation; note that older model cache blobs are re-encrypted on access in some flows which may affect latency for cold caches.
[00:09:30] Priya: That's fine, we just want to be aware. Data residency: our EU customers' data must never leave EU.
[00:09:38] Maya: You can pin region to EU for hosted, or run Private in your EU environment. We'll confirm region tagging in the metadata responses.

[00:10:45] Lena: Back to RBAC mapping — can you show an example of SCIM group mapping to Redwood roles?
[00:10:52] Jared: Sure. Example: Okta group "aurora_platform_ops" -> Redwood role "operator". Okta group "aurora_platform_admins" -> Redwood role "admin". SCIM sync would create local user records and attach role pointers. We also recommend an audit-only group for contractors which maps to limited viewer privileges.
[00:11:14] Tom: How do you handle group deletions or user removal? We can't accidentally revoke access if someone is moved between groups during reorg.
[00:11:21] Jared: We have a soft-delete grace window configurable (default 7 days) where removal triggers a pending revocation until confirmed. You can set it to immediate if you prefer. That helps with re-org churn.

[00:12:50] Priya: What about name changes and emails? We use email as identity but sometimes they change.
[00:12:56] Jared: SCIM handles identity updates; we map by immutable unique ID if your IdP provides one (OIDC sub or Okta user id). If you map by email, we recommend an update flow to re-bind accounts.

[00:14:18] Marcus: Compliance nit: need to show proof of separation of duties — can we restrict that only security team can change RBAC policies?
[00:14:25] Maya: Absolutely. RBAC for RBAC changes (meta-permission) is supported — only users in specific admin groups can edit role definitions and mappings. Those changes are logged with who/when and exported.

[00:15:48] Tom: Any latency or performance impact if we enable SCIM group sync at large scale? We have tens of thousands of users and many groups.
[00:15:56] Jared: SCIM provisioning is batched and we support delta syncs. For large orgs we recommend scoping to only the groups that are relevant to Redwood roles, and using group filters in Okta to limit pushes. Also use Dedicated/Dedicated+Burst if provisioning time matters since Dedicated gives you direct network locality.

[00:17:35] Priya: A question about encryption in transit between our Okta and Redwood — is SCIM always over TLS, any mutual TLS support?
[00:17:42] Jared: SCIM over TLS is required. We also support mTLS for Private/Dedicated customers — you can require a client cert on the provisioning endpoint. Hosted customers can use IP allow lists as an alternative.

[00:19:03] Lena: For SAML assertion attributes — what do you see as the minimum?
[00:19:08] Jared: Minimum: nameid/email and a persistent user id. Optionally a primary role. Groups ideally via SCIM. Also include eduPersonTargetedID/unique attributes if you have them.

[00:20:30] Maya: Quick note on SAML metadata lifecycle — our metadata includes endpoints and certificate expiry. We prefer you set up certificate rollover automation on Okta to avoid breaks.
[00:20:40] Tom: Ok — who rotates certs on your side?
[00:20:43] Jared: We rotate SP certs on a regular cadence and publish metadata with overlap. But we still ask customers to monitor metadata expiry and set reminders.

[00:22:10] Marcus: Do you provide SOC 2 artifacts and a point-in-time report we can attach to audits?
[00:22:15] Maya: Yes, for enterprise customers we share SOC 2, ISO attestations, and we can do a security questionnaire; for hosted customers it's via our compliance portal and for Private we provide a package for your auditors.

[00:23:52] Priya: On retention of PII in logs — we need to redact user emails in long-term archives. Is that possible?
[00:23:59] Jared: Yes you can configure PII redaction in logs before export. We can redact or pseudonymize emails and still keep user references in a hashed form to support forensics.

[00:25:10] Lena: Any gotchas we've seen with Okta + Redwood?
[00:25:15] Jared: A couple: 1) Okta's SCIM group push sometimes truncates group names over long syncs; keep names concise. 2) Relying solely on SAML role claims leads to stale permissions. 3) Expect initial flare of provisioning events on first sync — use a dry-run mode.

[00:26:40] Samir: Does Redwood support per-team namespace isolation or is it global? We want team-level separation for sensitive projects.
[00:26:48] Jared: You can create per-team namespaces, with scoped roles per namespace. That gives isolation and allows the same group mapping structure per namespace.

[00:28:05] Tom: We have an internal requirement that any admin key material must be rotated every 90 days and be KMS-wrapped. Does Redwood enforce rotation or is that customer-managed?
[00:28:14] Maya: We support both. For hosted we can enforce rotation schedules for API tokens and KMS wrap usage; for Private you manage the KMS lifecycle.

[00:29:30] Lena: Ok last major topic — emergency break-glass access. How do we configure that without violating least privilege?
[00:29:38] Jared: Break-glass is a separate role with very limited distribution, combined with mandatory approval and extra audit logging. We typically require a secondary approval (two-person) for the most sensitive actions and time-limited tokens recorded in the audit trail.

[00:31:00] Priya: Implementation details — how long does it take to onboard an Okta + SCIM + RBAC mapping into production for a team of our size?
[00:31:08] Jared: For a minimal pilot (10–50 users) 1–2 days. For full enterprise rollout with group mapping, audit configuration, and KMS integration expect 2–4 weeks depending on schedules and approvals.

[00:33:10] Maya: Let's capture concrete next steps. We'll send metadata and playbooks, you (Aurora) agree to a pilot window and share Okta SCIM token and list of groups to map.
[00:33:30] Tom: We'll try to get that token and group list by next week.
[00:33:36] Marcus: We'll need the SOC 2 package for audit evidence.
[00:33:40] Maya: I'll attach the SOC 2 cert and the compliance FAQ in the follow-up email.

[00:34:50] Jared: One more small note — we'll attach sample policy examples for temporary elevation and for contractor guest access.
[00:34:55] Priya: Great. Also include the steps for mTLS if we want mutual TLS on SCIM.

[00:36:00] Lena: Any blockers from our side?
[00:36:03] Tom: Need to coordinate Okta admin time. We have someone assigned but may need a dedicated window.
[00:36:10] Priya: We'll confirm internal tickets for rotation and KMS.

[00:37:25] Maya: Wrap up — recap: Redwood to send SAML SP metadata, SCIM provisioning playbook, RBAC mapping template, SOC 2 artifacts. Aurora to provide Okta SCIM token, list of groups to map, and confirm pilot window.
[00:37:42] Jared: I'll include sample CLI commands and a dry-run checklist to validate the first sync.

[00:38:10] Action items recap (read aloud):
- Maya: SP metadata, onboarding checklist, SOC 2 package.
- Jared: SCIM playbook, RBAC templates, dry-run checklist.
- Tom: Okta SCIM token + groups to map.
- Priya: Confirm KMS approach & data residency constraints.

[00:40:00] Questions (open):
- Confirm which groups map to admin/operator/viewer (assigned to Aurora).
- Decide on soft-delete grace window.
- Confirm whether PII redaction required in long-term logs.

[00:41:15] Closing notes:
Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with an invite for the pilot kickoff.
[00:41:22] Lena: Thanks, that was helpful.
[00:41:25] End call
